questions_before_times: What the chimney serves: a fireplace, a wood stove, an insert or a furnace
The fuel: wood, gas, pellet or oil
Any signs of an old chimney fire: puffy black flakes, a warped damper, cracked tiles
A home sale, a new stove or a new fuel (these make it a Level 2)
Any animals heard in the chimney
At the counter: which stove, and its maker if known
safety_stop: A chimney fire now: a loud roar, flames or sparks from the top, smoke filling the house
A carbon monoxide alarm, or a gas smell
license: Sweeping and inspecting a chimney has no state license in most places. Where a state or city licenses chimney or home repair work, its form asks for it. Repairs (caps, crowns, liners, rebuilds) can need a contractor license or registration where the state or city requires one. Gas stove and insert work needs a gas fitter's license where the state licenses gas work. The hearth shop's counter: business registration only.
